index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents an overview of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, depicted as a left-to-right data flow diagram. The global layout is linear and sequential, progressing from input on the far left to output on the far right, with distinct processing stages clearly labeled beneath each module. The structure consists of five main components: Input, two alternating Convolutional and Max Pooling layers, a Fully Connected Layer, and finally the Output layer.

Visual modules are represented using specific shapes and colors to denote their function. The Input is shown as three vertically stacked rectangular blocks—red, green, and blue—symbolizing a multi-channel input (e.g., RGB image), with the label 'Input' positioned below. Following this, the first Convolutional Layer is illustrated as a group of overlapping gray rectangles of varying shades, arranged in a staggered pattern to represent multiple feature maps generated by convolution operations; this group is labeled 'Convolutional Layer'. Next is the Max Pooling Layer, depicted similarly as a set of gray rectangles, but fewer in number and slightly larger, indicating downsampling; it is labeled 'Max Pooling Layer'. This sequence repeats: another Convolutional Layer followed by another Max Pooling Layer, both visually consistent with the first pair. After the second Max Pooling Layer, the network transitions to a Fully Connected Layer, represented by a vertical stack of light green circular nodes, each connected to all nodes in the preceding layer, signifying dense connectivity; this is labeled 'Fully Connected Layer'. Finally, the Output is shown as a vertical list of K labels (numbered 1 through K, with ellipses indicating intermediate values), each connected to one node from the Fully Connected Layer, representing a classification into K classes.

Connections between modules are drawn as thin gray lines, indicating the flow of data. From the Input, multiple lines fan out to each rectangle in the first Convolutional Layer, illustrating the application of multiple filters. Each subsequent layer connects fully to the next: every rectangle in the first Convolutional Layer connects to every rectangle in the first Max Pooling Layer, and so on. The transition from the second Max Pooling Layer to the Fully Connected Layer involves lines connecting each of the final feature map rectangles to every circular node in the Fully Connected Layer, emphasizing the flattening and full connectivity. From the Fully Connected Layer, each circular node connects to one output class label, forming a one-to-one mapping for classification. The diagram uses consistent line styles and spacing to maintain clarity and visual hierarchy, with labels placed directly beneath each major component for easy identification. The overall design emphasizes the hierarchical and feedforward nature of the CNN, from spatial feature extraction to final classification.
